title: COMPOSITE MONOLITH & DUAL ZOOM-FOCUS
subtitle: 7-Part Composite Architecture and Non-Breaking Bezier Camera Inspection
author: ARTIFICIAL CRAFT

pages.title: 01 // THE 7-PART MECHANICAL COMPOSITE
pages.content:
Monolithic blocks are boring if they are solid. Real mechanics have internal structure.

The Composite Monolith is an assembly of 7 optical and mechanical parts:
1. Beveled Outer Armor Plates.
2. Glowing Crystalline Neural Core.
3. Gold Logic Bus Interconnects.
4. Heatsink Dissipation Fins.
5. Dual Telemetry Ribbons.
6. 4-Corner Optical Laser Calipers.
7. Precision Machined Chassis.

pages.title: 02 // 0% TO 100% EXPLODED VIEW MATH
pages.content:
How do you dismantle a 3D machine on a web page? You don't swap pre-rendered videos. You interpolate vector offsets live in WebGL.

The Exploded View slider drives MathUtils.damp calculations. At 0%, a tight unibody chassis. At 100%, outer armor plates push outwards along normal vectors, exposing the neural core and gold logic interconnects without breaking spatial matrix bounds.

pages.title: 03 // NON-BREAKING DUAL ZOOM-FOCUS
pages.content:
In standard 3D web viewers, clicking an object jerks the camera and disorients the user. Our Dual Zoom-Focus Engine solves this:

• Director Auto-Fly Mode: Camera glides along closed Bezier curve paths through the tunnel.
• Inspection Focus Mode: Vector interpolation smoothly pulls camera target to selected Data Node while locking anchor state.

Resuming auto-flight restores original trajectory vectors smoothly with zero camera jitter.
